entry.title: The brown band across Mino: a shadow rendered before there was a figure
entry.content:
The brown band across Mino: a shadow rendered before there was a figure

ContactShadows sat beside the lights, so its frames={1} fired at mount while
the model was still suspended, and the demand loop left that uninitialised
render target on screen — a brown band across the character, wider than the
model because the shadow plane is. The rig now says when the figure is in
the scene and the shadow mounts then, keeping the single frame.

entry.title: EdNet-KT1: Sabelia wins the ranking, loses the calibration, and V1 fails
entry.content:
EdNet-KT1: Sabelia wins the ranking, loses the calibration, and V1 fails

Three seeds over 5,792 learners and 679k answers. 0.660 AUC against DKT's
0.655 and BKT's 0.635 — and 0.632 log loss against BKT's 0.622, with worse
ECE and worse accuracy. V1's exit condition asks for AUC *and* log loss
against the best baseline, so the engine has not cleared it. The earlier
claim that Duolingo had met V1 is corrected everywhere: one dataset is not
the bar the roadmap set.

The ablations lose their last excuse. EdNet has response times and 12,056
questions against 142 tags, so no_response and no_item are testing something
real here — and paired by seed, neither moves the same way on all three
seeds, nor does time, nor forgetting, on any of the three datasets. What
carries the result is attention over the concept sequence, which is not what
the four mechanisms were added for.

The one actionable finding points down, not up: dropping the item embedding
takes the model from 862k parameters to 90k without costing AUC.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Compare ablations within a seed, not across the means
entry.content:
Compare ablations within a seed, not across the means

The variants share their split, their initialisation and their batch order,
so what varies between seeds moves all of them together; a paired difference
sees through that. It does not rescue the ablations: on the synthetic set and
the Duolingo prefix every paired difference is inside 0.006 AUC and none has
the same sign on all three seeds. Three seeds cannot carry a significance
test, so the script prints the differences and their signs, not a p-value.

entry.title: Duolingo on whole learner histories: the lead narrows
entry.content:
Duolingo on whole learner histories: the lead narrows

Keeping every row of a 4% learner sample instead of the file's first 300k
rows raises the median sequence from 25 to 36 — and raises every model except
this one. The recency heuristic goes 0.604 to 0.621, DAS3H 0.603 to 0.626,
DKT 0.635 to 0.644, Sabelia 0.662 to 0.661, so its lead over the best
logistic baseline falls from 0.058 to 0.037. Longer histories help the simple
models more than they help the attention model, which is the opposite of the
argument for it.

The one thing that moved the right way: removing the time features now costs
something (0.657), where on the prefix it cost nothing. The forgetting gate
still scores higher without it. One seed — the run was stopped there to give
the machine to EdNet, which has the response times and distinct item ids that
decide the remaining ablations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Academic knowledge engine, Phase 4: one atlas, disagreement included
entry.content:
Academic knowledge engine, Phase 4: one atlas, disagreement included

Many lectures' extractions fold into one entry per concept. What folding
would destroy is what this keeps: confidence counts lectures rather than
repetitions, so twenty mentions in one lecture stay one lecture's word; a
concept no segment ever supported is capped low however often the model
produced it; and two sources defining a concept differently produce a record
instead of a vote, while one lecture rephrasing itself produces nothing.

Writing the tests found the API wart: a fixed list of existing concepts
cannot rank several candidates, because similarity belongs to a pair. The
lookup is now a function of one normalised key.

entry.title: The Sabelia Lab: the engine's results, inside the product, admin only
entry.content:
The Sabelia Lab: the engine's results, inside the product, admin only

A page that leads with the losses. It renders a frozen snapshot of the
benchmark runs — scripts/sabelia-snapshot.py writes it, the product never
calls the engine to draw a page — and labels what a table cannot carry: a
synthetic dataset says it validates the pipeline and not the model, a
one-seed table says a difference may be the seed, a dataset where a simple
baseline wins names the baseline, and ablation rows are marked so they are
not read as five models. It closes with what the engine's status actually
is: shadow, never shown to a learner.

entry.title: Academic knowledge engine, Phase 3: extraction with evidence and support
entry.content:
Academic knowledge engine, Phase 3: extraction with evidence and support

A segment becomes concepts, relations and claims that each carry the lecture
and the milliseconds they came from, and each carry source_supported or
inferred. Unmarked is stored as inferred: an unmarked object is one nobody
promised the segment carried, and calling it supported would launder the
thing the flag exists to show. A claim with no epistemic tag is dropped, a
relation into a concept the model never returned is dropped, and a segment
the segmenter flagged is never sent.

The script estimates the run before spending anything: 18.06 is about 1.07M
input tokens across its 1,164 segments. No model has read them — this
machine has no provider key — so the pipeline is proven against a fake
gateway that returns what models really return, including edges into
nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Sample EdNet learners by hash, not by lowest user id
entry.content:
Sample EdNet learners by hash, not by lowest user id

The lowest ids are the earliest registrations, so a prefix of them is a
cohort, not a sample. sample_users draws that many learners from the whole
set by a stable hash, records the draw in the dataset version, and is what
the benchmark config uses. EdNet is also the dataset that can settle what
Duolingo could not: it has response times and question ids distinct from
their tags, so the response and item ablations finally have something to
read.

entry.title: Academic knowledge engine, Phase 2: captions, cache, segments
entry.content:
Academic knowledge engine, Phase 2: captions, cache, segments

acquire.py fetches a registered lecture's official .vtt once, into a private
cache with a manifest that records where it came from, under which licence,
what it hashes to and when; a record whose trust or licence does not allow it
is skipped with the reason kept. captions.py parses WebVTT into cues, joins
them into sentences that carry the timing of their own words, and cuts those
into topic segments by lexical cohesion, flagging the ways a transcript lies.

The spoken-math flag is a density, not a keyword: at a mention of a matrix it
marked 82% of MIT 18.06, which says nothing. Calibrated on that course it
marks a third. Writing the tests found a real off-by-one — a sentence took
its end from the following cue, which would have pointed every citation one
caption late.

entry.title: Sabelia in shadow: recorded beside the Professor's decision, never ac…
entry.content:
Sabelia in shadow: recorded beside the Professor's decision, never acted on

The engine earned a benchmark, not a lesson. professor/shadow.py asks a
running Sabelia service what it would recommend and writes the answer into
the turn's decision record after the reply is streamed; it is off unless a
URL and the export secret are both set, and every failure is silent.
scripts/shadow-eval.py is the comparison that would justify moving it
inside: a prequential replay of an export scoring NOEMA's own rule against
the engine, which refuses to report below 500 graded events over 20
learners. The Duolingo adapter gains learner-level sampling so the whole
13M-row file can be read with the sequences at their real length. The Anki
import tests counted rows across the whole table and failed on any database
that was not pristine; they now count the test's own user's rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Sabelia on real data: the Duolingo HLR three-seed benchmark
entry.content:
Sabelia on real data: the Duolingo HLR three-seed benchmark

Every Sabelia variant reaches 0.661-0.664 AUC and 0.413 log loss on the
300k-row slice against 0.635 for DKT and 0.603 for DAS3H, spreads under
0.01, which meets V1's exit condition on one dataset. The five variants are
indistinguishable, so the time and forgetting components have no measured
gain there; README, technical report, model card, roadmap and the
integration plan say both things. benchmark_table.py's base-rate line read
the wrong dict and is fixed.

entry.title: Academic Source Registry: records, licences, trust, and the MIT OCW a…
entry.content:
Academic Source Registry: records, licences, trust, and the MIT OCW adapter

Phase 1 of the Academic Knowledge Engine. noema/academic/registry.py
holds the records a source must have before anything is derived from it
(university, course, instructors, content type, licence read from the
source, trust from an allow-list of official domains and YouTube channel
ids, the official captions and transcript URLs); noema/academic/ocw.py
reads OCW's machine-readable data.json for a course, its video gallery
and each lecture, and never invents a lecture it could not read.
scripts/academic-register.py writes the registry as JSONL.

The 18.06 pilot: 35 lecture videos, 35 with official .vtt captions and
transcript PDFs, all CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Nothing beyond metadata is fetched.

entry.title: Aquilante: the demo page — knowledge map, next action, recall curve, lab
entry.content:
Aquilante: the demo page — knowledge map, next action, recall curve, lab

A static HTML page built by scripts/build_demo.py from the library: a
simulated learner's state as a map (mastery radius, uncertainty ring,
prerequisite lines), the policy's recommendation with reason codes, the
half-life recall curve of the weakest concept against the review
threshold, the per-concept table, and the lab view with the recorded
benchmark and the fallback model's reliability diagram. Inline SVG, no
JavaScript; every number is computed at build time and the page says the
learner is simulated and which model produced the estimates.

entry.content:
Aquilante: the three-seed table, and that it settles nothing about the ablations

The benchmark script aggregates seeds (mean ± sample sd). On the
synthetic set with three seeds the ranking holds — heuristic, PFA, BKT,
DKT, then the Aquilante variants — and the spread (about 0.025 AUC) is
larger than every gap, so the README says plainly that the ablations are
undecided here and will be decided on real-time data.
